name: Bosnia and Herzegovina

fees.name: Short-stay visa (Type C), single entry
fees.validity: up to 90 days in any 180-day period
fees.applies: nationalities requiring a visa; fee as published by BiH Embassy in Washington DC
fees.notes: Fees are set centrally in EUR by BiH regulation but published by each embassy in local currency, so amounts vary by mission: BiH Embassy Washington DC lists USD 39 single / USD 70 multiple; BiH Embassy Amman lists USD 71 for Visa C. The central MFA (mfa.gov.ba) fee schedule was unreachable at time of research. Applicants must apply at a BiH diplomatic/consular mission - there is no e-visa.

fees.name: Short-stay visa (Type C), multiple entry
fees.validity: up to 90 days in any 180-day period, multiple entries
fees.applies: nationalities requiring a visa; fee as published by BiH Embassy in Washington DC
fees.notes: BiH Embassy Amman also lists USD 71 for multiple-entry Visa C; amounts vary by embassy.

fees.name: Long-stay visa (Type D)
fees.validity: long stay (over 90 days), typically up to 6 months
fees.applies: all applicants requiring a Type D visa; fee as published by BiH Embassy in Amman
fees.notes: Type D covers long-stay purposes including business assignments; embassy-issued only. Amount varies by mission.

fees.name: Transit visa (Type B)
fees.notes: Transit visa exists but no fee amount was published on the official embassy pages consulted; amount not verified so left null.

vfs.note: Bosnia and Herzegovina does not outsource inbound visa applications to VFS Global/TLScontact/BLS; applications are lodged directly at BiH embassies and consulates. (VFS centres located inside BiH serve outbound travellers applying for UK/Canada/Schengen visas, not visas to BiH.)

free_visa_notes: Bosnia and Herzegovina is NOT a Schengen member; Schengen fees do not apply. Citizens of the EU/EEA, USA, UK, and many other countries enter visa-free for up to 90 days. No e-visa or standard visa-on-arrival programme exists; visas are issued at BiH diplomatic missions (border issuance only in exceptional, justified humanitarian cases under BiH law). No published nationality-based reciprocity fee schedule was found; fee differences observed are per-embassy currency conversions rather than reciprocity.
